_what: Amendment 1 to the M0c Session A pre-registration. Adds one arm that the original file did not contain, and records why it exists and when it was written.
written_before: any held-out number for this session. The held-out split has NOT been opened for R@1 by any arm at the time this file is written.

why_an_amendment_and_not_a_quiet_additio._the_honest_account: The original registration named four ranking arms (L1, L2, S1, S2) and one selector (C1). All four ranking arms were built and cross-validated and ALL FOUR ARE NULL. The arm added here -- slate construction -- was not in the original file. It was found by R3, a diagnostic run AFTER the original registration, which measured that the shipped depth-10 slate is not the best way to choose which ten candidates the cross-encoder sees.
why_an_amendment_and_not_a_quiet_additio._the_risk_this_creates: An arm added mid-session, after four registered arms failed, is exactly the shape of a post-hoc selection. Session J's addendum is the precedent: the post-hoc length form looked strongest on fit and FAILED its registered floor on every held-out cell. That is what post-hoc selection predicts and it is why this amendment carries its own floor and its own prediction, written now.
why_an_amendment_and_not_a_quiet_additio._what_is_NOT_being_done: No floor is being lowered. Number 1's floor stays at +0.02 held-out R@1. The four original arms are reported as the nulls they measured, not quietly dropped.

a_disclosure_that_belongs_in_the_record.what_happened: tools/reach_head_r3_slate.py was run on the HELD-OUT split before it was run on fit. It measures input recall of the already-published configuration under alternative slate orderings and fits no parameter, but it was seen.
a_disclosure_that_belongs_in_the_record.why_it_is_disclosed_rather_than_absorbed: the project's standing rule is that a measurement taken is a measurement reported. A reader who finds the held-out R3 output in runs/session-m0c/ and no mention of it in the record would be right to distrust the rest.
a_disclosure_that_belongs_in_the_record.how_the_selection_was_protected: the selection below is made ENTIRELY on the fit split, by the tie-break rule already written in the original registration. The held-out R3 read and the fit R3 read DISAGREE in direction on the single strongest rule -- dense-ordered top-10 is worse than gate on fit (0.9083 vs 0.9214) and better on held-out (0.9258 vs 0.9039) -- which is itself the evidence that selecting on the held-out read would have been selecting on noise.
a_disclosure_that_belongs_in_the_record.residual_risk_stated_plainly: non-zero. The union family was visible as promising in both R3 outputs. The mitigation is that the specific rule and depth were chosen by a pre-written tie-break on fit numbers, and that the floor below was set before the read.

arm_S3_slate_construction.what: the depth-10 rerank slate is built as the UNION of the gate order's top 8 and the dense cue's top 8, instead of the gate order's top 10.
arm_S3_slate_construction.the_reranker_is_UNCHANGED: same graph, same digest 9c222dac..., same f32, same seq 256, same batch 1, same depth. Only which candidates reach it changes.
arm_S3_slate_construction.why_it_is_not_the_closed_fusion: ADR-010 and ADR-011 close fusion over per-cue scores DECIDING THE RANKING -- 'no fusion over per-cue scores can fix cue selection at rank 1; the top-1 either-cue oracle is 0.652 and that is the exact ceiling on perfect arbitration'. A union combines no scores and arbitrates nothing: every admitted candidate is ranked by the cross-encoder, which already scores 0.6725 against that 0.6463 oracle precisely because it is not arbitrating between cues. The closed item is a RANKING mechanism; this is an ADMISSION rule. This distinction must land in DECISIONS.md before anything ships, and if a reader rejects it the arm does not ship.
arm_S3_slate_construction.latency: ZERO added cost. The slate is the same size, so the same ten pair passes run. The union is two integer top-k selections over arrays the retriever already has.

fit_measurement_that_selected_it.control_check: gate top10 reproduces the published fit R@1 0.7555 exactly

selection_by_the_ALREADY_WRITTEN_tie_bre.the_rule_quoted_from_the_original_file: Ties within 0.005 are broken by measured added latency, lowest wins.
selection_by_the_ALREADY_WRITTEN_tie_bre.arithmetic: 0.0131 - 0.0087 = 0.0044, which is inside 0.005, so gate9 UNION dense9 and gate8 UNION dense8 are a TIE under the pre-written rule. gate8 UNION dense8 adds zero latency; gate9 UNION dense9 adds one pair pass.
selection_by_the_ALREADY_WRITTEN_tie_bre._why_both_are_declared: the held-out tool scores every rule in one pass. Declaring which one is PRIMARY before the read is what stops that pass from being a fishing expedition. Every other rule in the output is context and none of them is quotable as this session's result.

floor._unchanged: shipped 0.6725 + 0.02, exactly as number_1 registered it. An arm below this FAILS OUTRIGHT and does not ship.
floor._expected_to_fail: stated plainly: the fit delta is +0.0087 and the registered calibration-generalization prediction is that held-out deltas come in BELOW fit deltas. The honest expectation is that S3 does NOT clear its floor. It is read anyway, because a measured small positive reported as small is worth more than an unmeasured hope.

bands.directional_prediction: input recall rises and conditional accuracy falls partly to meet it, so the R@1 delta is materially smaller than the recall delta. Measured on fit: +0.0131 recall bought +0.0087 R@1; +0.0262 recall bought +0.0043.
bands.what_would_falsify_the_directional_predi: a held-out R@1 delta at least as large as the input-recall delta. That would mean the added candidates are not adding distractors, and the fit reading of the mechanism is wrong.

preconditions_of_the_heldout_read.control_must_reproduce: gate top10 must reproduce held-out R@1 0.6725 exactly, or no delta measured against it means anything. Enforced in code -- the tool refuses to write.
preconditions_of_the_heldout_read.adr_010_reach: S3 changes which candidates are scored, so it can change top-1 by construction; the fit-measured count is reported.

adr_014_power.test: two-sided exact McNemar over queries whose top-1 differs
adr_014_power.contrast_the_test_consumes: gate8 UNION dense8 top-1 vs gate top10 top-1, SAME reranker, same split, same 229 population
adr_014_power.if_below_the_floor: alpha declared UNATTAINABLE and the delta carries the verdict alone

the_four_original_ranking_arms_as_measur._recorded_here_so_the_amendment_cannot_b: all four were built, cross-validated by conversation over the fit split, and reported. None is dropped.

L1_listwise_finetune._reading: a NULL WITH POWER, and slightly negative

the_four_original_ranking_arms_as_measur.the_conclusion_registered_before_the_hel: learned re-scoring of the existing depth-10 slate does not generalise from this fit split. Four architectures spanning a 384-dimensional pooled bottleneck to full token-level cross-attention all land on the shipped number. The binding constraint is the DATA: 229 fit queries of which 38 are recoverable failures, on a reranker Session J already fine-tuned on those same queries.

what_this_amendment_does_not_do.does_not_lower_a_floor: number_1's floor is +0.02 held-out and stays there.
what_this_amendment_does_not_do.does_not_claim_the_named_candidates_succ: candidate A is negative and candidate B is null. Both are reported as measured.
what_this_amendment_does_not_do.does_not_ship_anything: shipping requires clearing the floor, a DECISIONS entry for the admission-rule distinction, a Rust implementation reproducing the Python read exactly, and every standing check.
